I was worried about how this interacts with https://github.com/whatwg/fs/issues/39, but I guess with directories, unlike with files, there's no way to re-create the directory once it's been removed without access to the parent (which is impossible in this case). So yeah, specifying that the next invocation of `navigator.storage.getDirectory()` creates a new OPFS seems reasonable. 

This also solves an existing problem in the Chromium implementation (mentioned in https://github.com/whatwg/fs/issues/59) where handles in the OPFS could become suddenly valid if the path is re-created from underneath it. By creating a new OPFS instance, all handles pointing to the old instance are guaranteed to never become valid again

body:
Hmm. The "request access" check should happen before attempting to take the lock, and we shouldn't bother attempting to take the lock unless the "request access" check succeeds. So I'm not sure how this would fit into the `lockResultAlgorithm`?

Should we also post the "request access" algorithm as a task? Something like:
```
(in parallel)
1. Let |lockResultAlgorithm| be an algorithm which takes a |lockResult| and
     runs these steps:
  <do file system operations>
  ...

1. Let |accessResultAlgorithm| be an algorithm which takes an |accessResult| and
     runs these steps:
  1. Reject |result| if not "granted"
  1. Take a lock on |entry| with |lockResultAlgorithm|.

1. Queue a storage task given |entry|'s relevant global object and |entry|'s request
   access algorithm with a value of "readwrite", returning the result to |accessResultAlgorithm|.
```
